replacement: Replace the static badge with one derived from the package metadata (a shields.io PyPI pyversions badge for pyeye-mcp), or drop it and state the floor through a fact block for project.requires_python.

problem: The numbered loading order stops at auto-discovery, but load_config applies a fifth source last: the session's unsaved configure_packages(save=False) additions (#953), which are merged over everything and don't suppress auto-discovery. A reader who calls configure_packages without saving can't tell from this list where those entries land.
replacement: Bind the loading order as a fact generated from ProjectConfig.load_config, so the session overlay from configure_packages(save=False) appears as the last step, instead of the hand-numbered list.

problem: Item 4 says auto-discovery detects source layouts and sibling packages. That is right except on one path: when a src/ layout is found, _auto_discover returns early and adds no sibling packages. It also omits that, without src/, it adds virtualenv site-packages (venv/, .venv/, env/) alongside siblings.
replacement: 4. **Auto-Discovery**: if no packages are configured, a `src/` layout is used when present; otherwise sibling packages and the project's virtualenv site-packages are added.
route_reason: Library behaviour of ProjectConfig with no MCP tool that demonstrates it, so no example route; no extractor covers discovery order.

problem: The section says pyeye detects src layouts from pyproject.toml build-backend metadata. That is right except on two paths: pyproject.toml is read only when it is the first project config file found (a .pyeye.json/.pyeye.yaml/.pyeye.yml in the root means it is never read), and detection is skipped when packages are already set, including by the global config. A user with a global `packages` list gets no build-backend detection and no src/ fallback.
replacement: Add after the intro: "Detection reads pyproject.toml only when it is the project's config file (no `.pyeye.json` or `.pyeye.yaml` in the root), and only when no `packages` are set yet, including by your global config."
route_reason: Config-loading behaviour of ProjectConfig with no MCP tool example to show it and no extractor for it.

problem: Says the flag registers `get_performance_metrics`; it registers every admin tool in ADMIN_TOOLS, which also includes get_connection_diagnostics. 'Set' is also loose for a boolean variable that registers nothing when set to false.
replacement: Set `PYEYE_ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_METRICS` to true to register the admin tools, <fact block for tools.admin>. Their parameters are in the [tool reference](docs/reference/tools.md#admin-tools).

problem: The `.mcp.json` runs a bare `python`, resolved from the PATH of whatever launched the client, so the server uses the project venv only when the client was started from a shell with that venv active; the page itself says so for env vars and for other clients.
replacement: Set `command` to your venv's Python (e.g. `/path/to/your/project/venv/bin/python`) so the server runs in your project's environment; a bare `python` works only when the client is launched from a shell with that venv active.
subject: This way, the MCP server uses your project's environment and has access to all your project's dependencies.
